## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 70 (titled *Sahajīvinī-avūpakāsana*, "Not sending away a new disciple") is a monastic disciplinary rule concerning the treatment of a newly ordained pupil (*sahajīvinī*) [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun who confers ordination (*vuṭṭhāpana*) upon a student without subsequently taking her away commits an offense requiring confession [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009]. Specifically, the preceptor is required to take her pupil away for a distance of at least five or six *yojanas* [Sujato 2009; Entrance to the Vinaya 1983].

According to the origin story, this measure was instituted because the husband of an ordained woman sought to retrieve her [Sujato 2009]. Removing the newly ordained nun from her husband's locality was intended to protect her from being forcefully reclaimed, reflecting the legal reality that a husband could attempt to compel his wife to return even after her entry into the monastic order [Entrance to the Vinaya 1983; Hüsken 1997]. In the commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*), the verbal form *vūpakāsetabbo* is explained as taking the person elsewhere (*aññattha netabbo*) [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra (both Pc 70), as well as corresponding rules in the Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 122), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 160), Mahāsāṅghika (Bi Vb Pc 108), and Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda (Bi Vb Pc 108) traditions [SuttaCentral]. Sujato observes that the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya lacks an equivalent for this rule [Sujato 2009]. DharmaNexus records 316 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 78 texts, showing substantial shared formulaic text with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 34, 68, and 78, and automatically aligns passages with the Tibetan *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106) [DharmaNexus].
